attempts.observation: The first full matrix was stopped after the original per-resource cleanup implementation made the 512-resource browser boundary non-viable; no raw output was published.
Callbacks completed in approximately 242 ms, but repeated ledger searches and mutation consumed approximately 67.6 seconds.
A single batch release removed repeated searches but still rebuilt oversized maps and history.
Bounded ledger history exposed successful-row sanitization as the next scaling cost.
Ordering accounted for 97 ms and did not explain the remaining amplification.
Successful rows stopped carrying force-only fields and the Chrome boundary passed.
Chrome retained 220 samples with 22 deadline failures, including all maximum-payload 512 samples; Firefox reached the 600-second harness timeout before returning its sample vector.
Firefox completed only 448 lease callbacks before the deadline.
The external-size primitive itself stalled the AtomVM measurement; the probe was interrupted and byte instrumentation was changed to explicit unavailable on AtomVM.
Removing byte instrumentation reduced observer effect but did not satisfy the deadline.
One provider call per page passed Chrome but showed that Firefox time was dominated by duplicate result materialization rather than provider callbacks.
Direct page-to-report collation passed Chrome with substantial margin; Firefox still exhausted the deadline after seven lease pages, so Phase 13 remains revise.

A second clean pinned build reproduced the semantic result: Chrome completed 513 callbacks in eight lease pages with zero unresolved; Firefox completed 448 callbacks in seven lease pages and retained 65 unresolved identities.
Both engines pass 64, 65, and 256 resources with exact terminal state. Chrome passes 512; Firefox stops after seven pages and retains 65 unresolved identities.
